clue.text: Big waves beyond territorial waters

definitions.meaning: tall, rough waves at sea, the swell running high
the open ocean outside any nation's jurisdiction

explanation.surface: Huge breakers roll in from the open ocean far offshore.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough water is described as a heavy sea running tall, and international waters outside national limits carry the same two-word name.

clue.text: Concealing a drubbing

explanation.surface: Someone hides a beating they took.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiding is both the act of keeping out of sight and a slang word for a severe thrashing.

clue.text: Her husband prefers greens

parts.note: greens are not vegetables but putting greens on a course; the wife is neglected for the game

explanation.definitionFit: A woman whose spouse spends all his free time on the links is jokingly called widowed by the sport.

clue.text: Massacre almost developing from such wounding words

indicators.note: developing means the remaining letters change into a new form
almost means the word massacre loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A massacre grows out of cutting remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts MASSACRE to MASSACR, which 'developing' rearranges. 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcasm is bitter, cutting irony, its name from Greek for tearing flesh.

clue.text: Some are plagued with malaria

indicators.note: some means only part of the word plagued is taken

explanation.surface: Several people are troubled by a tropical fever.
explanation.definitionFit: Ague is an old name for malarial fever, so agued means suffering from that fever.

clue.text: Graduate's research place backs ointment

indicators.note: backs means the graduate's degree and the research place are both read in reverse, right to left

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate; with the possessive S it gives MAS
a lab, or laboratory, is a place for research

explanation.surface: A graduate's laboratory sponsors a new healing cream.
explanation.walkthrough: One indicator, 'backs', turns the whole run MAS + LAB, giving BAL + SAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsam is an aromatic resin used as a soothing healing salve.

clue.text: Archdeacon wearing bizarre gear — but he will get his own back

definitions.text: he will get his own back

indicators.note: wearing means the archdeacon is inside, dressed in the other letters
bizarre means the letters of gear are twisted into a strange order

parts.note: Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: A churchman in strange clothes plans revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Archdeacon' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it only supplies the title Venerable, abbreviated; the anagram made by 'bizarre' is AGER, which 'wearing' wraps round it.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenger is someone who takes revenge for a wrong.

clue.text: Exhausted swan is in the way

indicators.note: is in means the swan goes inside the way

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: A tired swan blocks the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent means used up, tired out.

clue.text: Many taking English need to avail themselves of a rubber

indicators.note: taking means the many is followed by English

parts.note: a mass is a great many
to use something is to avail oneself of it

explanation.surface: Lots of English folk want a pencil eraser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'need to' is a link. 'rubber' means one who rubs, not an eraser.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseuse is a woman who gives massages, literally one who rubs.

clue.text: Conventional manner captivates one's daughter

indicators.note: captivates means the manner holds the next piece captive inside it

parts.note: style is a manner or way
one is I, so one's gives IS

explanation.surface: A traditional style charms someone's daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylised art follows formal conventions rather than realism.

clue.text: With us, idle merriment produces the shakes

indicators.note: produces suggests the letters of us and idle merriment are worked into something new

explanation.surface: Idle merriment with friends ends in the trembling of a drunkard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' is a link word; the fifteen letters of US IDLE MERRIMENT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Delirium tremens is the trembling and hallucination of alcohol withdrawal, colloquially called the shakes.

clue.text: Unusual spread — unlike the curate's egg

parts.note: something new is novel, unusual
laid as in laid out, spread, like a table that is laid

explanation.surface: An odd spread on the table, quite different from a stale breakfast egg.
explanation.walkthrough: The curate's egg comes from a Punch cartoon: a timid curate served a bad egg says parts of it are excellent. A fresh egg is its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: The curate's egg was stale; a fresh one, just produced by the hen, is its contrary.

clue.text: Member having a peg — he gets what's left

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
a golf tee is the small peg the ball sits on

explanation.surface: A man with a wooden leg is the beneficiary of what remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what's left' means what is left in a will, not leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: A legatee is a beneficiary, someone who receives a bequest under a will.

clue.text: Ancient nomadic race, originally semi-toed

indicators.note: originally hints that the letters of semi-toed were first in some other order

explanation.surface: An old wandering tribe was said to have half-formed toes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edomites were a Biblical Semitic people, descendants of Esau, living south of the Dead Sea.

clue.text: Food here is removed before it can be eaten

definitions.text: Food here is removed before it can be eaten

parts.words: Food here is removed before it can be eaten
parts.note: the meal is carried off from the shop to be eaten elsewhere

explanation.definitionFit: Takeaway is food bought ready-cooked from a shop and taken home to eat.

clue.text: Pages and pages about a handwritten document

parts.note: re means about, concerning
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a handwritten document

explanation.surface: A long manuscript runs to page after page.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is a large quantity of paper, so reams means a great deal of writing.

clue.text: Arrival by river is a risky undertaking

parts.note: an advent is an arrival or coming
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Arriving by boat is a perilous enterprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' sets the pieces side by side; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventure is an exciting, hazardous enterprise.

clue.text: Special line, chopped-up Jamaica pepper

indicators.note: chopped-up means the letters are cut and mixed

explanation.surface: A special cut of Caribbean pepper.
explanation.definitionFit: Allspice is the dried berry of a West Indian tree, also called pimento or Jamaica pepper.

clue.text: Look sullen, being let down

definitions.meaning: to frown or scowl, rhyming with power
..., brought down, as a flag on a rope

explanation.surface: Someone scowls with disappointment after being let down.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: one rhymes with 'power', the other with 'mower'.
explanation.definitionFit: To scowl is to glower in one pronunciation, and something dropped by rope is brought down in the other.

clue.text: Pity about the Inspector!

parts.note: re means about, concerning
Inspector Morse is the Oxford detective of Colin Dexter's novels and the TV series

explanation.surface: Someone feels sorry for the detective.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is a famous British TV detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Pity in the sense of regret or sorrow over what was done matches contrition.

clue.text: Deceive sweetheart about source of gift, using great diplomacy

parts.note: to kid is to tease or deceive

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, so its opening letter

parts.note: about here means next to, the letter coming round the front of the sweetheart

explanation.surface: Someone fibs to a lover about where a present came from, very tactfully.
explanation.walkthrough: Kid gloves are soft leather gloves; handling with kid gloves means treating gently.
explanation.definitionFit: Kid-glove treatment is extremely tactful, gentle handling.

clue.text: A horse covered with fat is a dawdler

indicators.note: covered with means the fat wraps round the other letters

parts.note: lard is pig fat
gee-gee, GG, is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: A fat-smeared horse is a slow mover.
explanation.definitionFit: A laggard is one who falls behind, slow and lingering.

clue.text: Following unfinished business, this is the remnant

indicators.note: unfinished means the business word loses its final letter

parts.note: an agenda is a list of business to be dealt with

explanation.surface: After incomplete affairs, this is what remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this is' is a link. Fag end is British slang for a cigarette butt, and by extension the last scrappy part of anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A fag end is the last worthless part, like a cigarette stub.

clue.text: Look over cursorily and object about Asian shrub

parts.note: to skim is to read quickly and superficially

indicators.note: about means the word for object is turned round

parts.note: an aim is an object or goal

explanation.surface: Someone glances over a document and protests concerning an Asian bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimmia is an evergreen shrub from East Asia with red berries.

clue.text: Information needed in raising sheep

indicators.note: raising, in a down clue, means the sheep word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: Advice needed by someone breeding sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is data or information fed into a system.

clue.text: Battlefield is a magnet for tourism

indicators.note: for tourism suggests the letters go touring, moving about, so a magnet is rearranged

explanation.surface: A historic battle site draws visitors like a magnet.
explanation.walkthrough: Magenta in northern Italy was the site of the 1859 battle that gave the colour its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta is the Italian town where French and Sardinian forces beat the Austrians in 1859.

clue.text: Impersonate consumptive girl with cold

parts.note: Mimi is the seamstress dying of consumption in Puccini's opera La Boheme
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A girl with tuberculosis plays someone else while she has a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: To mimic is to copy someone's manner or voice.

clue.text: Length of beard — in feet, perhaps

indicators.note: of here places the beard word before the length word, as in a beard's measure

parts.note: an imperial is a small pointed beard below the lower lip, named for Napoleon III
a length is a measure

explanation.surface: Someone asks how long a beard is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' says feet is just one example of the old British system of units.
explanation.definitionFit: Feet belong to the old British system of units, alongside inches, yards and miles.

clue.text: Value of two quarters with back pay

indicators.note: with means the next part is joined on after the two letters

parts.note: E and S are compass points, quarters of the compass
E and S are compass points, quarters of the compass

indicators.note: back means the word for pay is read in reverse

parts.note: to meet a bill is to pay it

explanation.surface: Worth is reckoned as half a year's back pay.
explanation.definitionFit: To value something highly is to hold it in high regard, a verb sense of esteem.

clue.text: A police superintendent exposes drug user

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
a head is a superintendent, one in charge

explanation.surface: A senior detective unmasks someone taking narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposes' is a link word meaning reveals.
explanation.definitionFit: An acidhead is slang for a habitual taker of LSD.
